name: OpenAI Agents SDK
runtime_note: Normal model-backed runs require a configured model/provider. The official OpenAI quickstart uses OPENAI_API_KEY.
strengths: Built-in tools, guardrails, handoffs, sessions, tracing, and MCP support
watch_items: Default OpenAI model path requires API credentials and usage
Provider behavior can differ when using non-OpenAI models
Higher-level runtime means some loop behavior is managed for you

name: LangGraph
runtime_note: Graphs can run deterministic local nodes without an LLM. Model and tool integrations are chosen separately.
strengths: Fine-grained control over explicit state and control flow
Durable execution and human-in-the-loop are core orchestration concepts
watch_items: Lower-level abstraction means more orchestration code is owned by the developer
Tool/model ergonomics often come from adjacent LangChain integrations
Tracing commonly uses LangSmith rather than being the graph runtime itself

name: Pydantic AI
runtime_note: Production model runs require a configured provider, but official testing guidance supports TestModel and FunctionModel to avoid live model calls.
strengths: Official TestModel and FunctionModel support for offline tests
watch_items: Some orchestration capabilities rely on integrations rather than one built-in runtime
Pydantic AI and Pydantic Graph solve different layers of the problem
